# INDEX_RULES.md — Global Rules & Doc Routing

**Doc link:** <https://github.com/brando90/agents-config/blob/main/INDEX_RULES.md>

**TLDR:** Read this compact contract at task start, then read only the detailed rule sections whose triggers apply. All agents use the same policy; client-specific loading differs.

## How to load these rules

Refresh `~/agents-config` with `git -C ~/agents-config pull --ff-only` at each new non-trivial task and after an hour; preserve dirty/concurrent work and use the local copy if offline. Reread this index and relevant changed rules. When editing agents-config in an isolated checkout, use that checkout's index and detail files after refreshing the home checkout.

All Hard Rule **Details** links and matching Trigger Rule/Guideline links are mandatory routing: **before the action they govern, read that detail section and its applicable workflow**, including secret overrides, spending and review decisions. Do not read every topic file. Rule numbers are stable; paths below resolve beneath `~/agents-config/` (or the active agents-config checkout). If files are unavailable locally, fetch the same path under `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brando90/agents-config/main/`. A Markdown link is a reading instruction, not proof the client loaded it. Never eagerly import this index or the detail collection into an entry file; read them as task files.

Hard rules govern conflicts with older wording in a triggered procedure. Explicit user instructions and platform/tool constraints retain their normal precedence. The SNAP pre-approval in Trigger Rule 51 is scoped to authorized work and existing budgets. Detail pages retain the procedures, examples and exceptions; the catalog is optional lookup.

## Hard Rules (every response, never skip)

1. **Protect secrets.** Never commit credentials; inspect the exact staged diff and filenames before committing or pushing. Do not print secret values. Stop on a suspected leak and rotate exposed credentials; references/env vars replace embedded secrets. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-1)

2. **Sync, then verify before pushing.** `git fetch` first; if upstream moved, rebase and re-test; never force-push a shared branch. Never fabricate unavailable source content; mark it unresolved. Inspect the diff and run the relevant deterministic checks. Report actual evidence and limitations, not an untested success claim. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-2)

3. **Quality assurance (QA) is opt-in.** Only a tier Brando explicitly requests or sets for this work in a runbook, `[qa]`/`[light-qa]`/`[mega-qa]` commit tag or environment flag starts a model reviewer. Hooks, project files and older “QA required” text are not opt-in. “Do QA”/“light QA” means one opposite-company round; apply findings and verify without automatic re-review. Mega QA follows Trigger Rule 10. Hooks cannot impose unsolicited QA; do not mention QA when unrequested. Benchmark-reference acceptance (43) remains separate. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-3)

4. **Response ending and titles.** Compact results: 1–2 sentences plus `.md`/`gdoc` links. End `**TLDR-end:** [proj: task]` with 1–2 sentences (`[proj]` without a task); never open `TLDR-start`. Emails/status reports also end `TLDR-end:` before any signature; include real decisions/deadlines only. Name and restate the core deliverable, not a micro-step (optional `›` suffix). Research updates open with a copy-ready status sentence; results also include a 1–2 sentence collaborator message in Brando’s voice. Match owned titles to verified summaries, identifier first. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-4)

5. **Snapshot.** In chat, immediately after the closing summary, show `**Snapshot:**` with the smallest real artifact sample (normally 5–15 lines, at most 25), or say why nothing tangible exists. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-5)

6. **Refresh configuration.** Follow the task-start/hourly refresh above, reread relevant changes, and preserve other owners’ work. Shared edits belong in both entry points. Review remains opt-in under Hard Rule 3. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-6)

7. **Keep clients current.** Use the installed package manager and the supported update hook; never assume npm. Do not install/use the deprecated Gemini CLI. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-7)

8. **Models, budgets and acceptance.** Masters: Codex `gpt-6-astra` / `ultra`; Claude `claude-fable-5-1` / `max`. Keep configured defaults; explicitly select proportionate execution workers (experiment selection: Guideline 19). Verify actual models/efforts and billing route (subscription or in-scope provider key). Never buy credits, enable new charges or weaken acceptance to recover. Required models/families and scientific pins remain binding. Before dispatch/review, read this detail and Rule 48. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-8)

9. **Model access: CLIs, subscriptions and provider keys are allowed.** Agents may wire Brando's existing provider keys into agent clients, write provider application programming interface (API) calls and run key-loading scripts without asking. Load keys at runtime, never print or commit them, keep each within its owner's scope and existing budgets, and cap and cost-estimate key-billed batch or unattended runs. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-9)

10. **Explain terminology.** Expand every acronym, metric symbol and project-specific term on first use in each response, chat included; use descriptive names, not opaque internal labels. For Brando, a code may lead if a short gloss follows on first use. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-10)

11. **Numbers with verdicts.** Compact entries link full statistics (Rule 4). Give measured values, scales, denominators/splits, threshold sources, missing measurements. Statistical headlines need 95% intervals (resampling unit, limits) and `x [lo, hi] p-val=Z` (named test/null or `p-val=n/a`). Report correlations individually; when interpreting score levels, add absolute agreement and mean bias (judge minus human, positive = lenient) with both means. Give repeated-score variability/counts. Existing data only; read the statistics workflow first. Research precision (10-24-2026): read settings, definitions, numbers from the repo, run records or paper; `unknown` only after a named-path search (in caption). VeriBench tables carry a Pi + best open-weight row. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-11)

## Guidelines (best practices)

- [14](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-14): Complete direct authorized requests; do not ask again for already-authorized actions.
- [15](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-15): Read only task-relevant referenced docs.
- [16](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-16): Keep index, README and paths accurate; mirror shared entry bodies; verify actual host instruction files and reload state.
- [17](rules/responses.md#guideline-rule-17): Use anchored paths in prose and commands.
- [18](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-18): Use `ls -la` for configuration/credential directories.
- [19](rules/research.md#guideline-rule-19): Select experiment models/judges by capability, total cost and validation; preserve pins.
- [20](rules/responses.md#guideline-rule-20): Messages/drafts as Brando use his concise first-person voice; email includes required routing/signature.
- [21](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-21): Check `~/keys/` for credentials, model-provider keys included, before asking; keep values transient.
- [22](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-22): Let the Node version manager control its path; avoid hardcoded versioned PATH entries.
- [23](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-23): Authorized email: Brando's signed-in account (mail connector, else uutils SMTP); BCC three inboxes, sender and To included; visible CC only on request; `drafted with <agent>` sign-off; “send” means send.
- [24](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-24): Paper PDFs follow mandatory Rule 35.
- [25](rules/research.md#guideline-rule-25): VeriBench/VB private: >0.98 saturated; ≤0.9 good, ≤0.5 great, 0 best. "Harsh metric", N tasks, ASCII, harness. vb-priv: SYNC.md. Any metric ≥~0.98: solved (heuristic). [Set names](workflows/vb-sets.md).

4. **Response ending and titles.** Compact results: 1–2 sentences plus `.md`/`gdoc` links. End `**TLDR-end:** [proj: task]` with 1–2 sentences (`[proj]` without a task); never open `TLDR-start`. Emails/status reports also end `TLDR-end:` before any signature; include real decisions/deadlines only. Name and restate the core deliverable, not a micro-step (optional `›` suffix). Research updates open with a copy-ready status sentence; results also include a 1–2 sentence collaborator message in Brando’s voice. Match owned titles to verified summaries, identifier first. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-4)

5. **Snapshot.** In chat, immediately after the closing summary, show `**Snapshot:**` with the smallest real artifact sample (normally 5–15 lines, at most 25), or say why nothing tangible exists. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-5)

6. **Refresh configuration.** Follow the task-start/hourly refresh above, reread relevant changes, and preserve other owners’ work. Shared edits belong in both entry points. Review remains opt-in under Hard Rule 3. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-6)

7. **Keep clients current.** Use the installed package manager and the supported update hook; never assume npm. Do not install/use the deprecated Gemini CLI. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-7)

8. **Models, budgets and acceptance.** Masters: Codex `gpt-6-astra` / `ultra`; Claude `claude-fable-5-1` / `max`. Keep configured defaults; explicitly select proportionate execution workers (experiment selection: Guideline 19). Verify actual models/efforts and billing route (subscription or in-scope provider key). Never buy credits, enable new charges or weaken acceptance to recover. Required models/families and scientific pins remain binding. Before dispatch/review, read this detail and Rule 48. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-8)

9. **Model access: CLIs, subscriptions and provider keys are allowed.** Agents may wire Brando's existing provider keys into agent clients, write provider application programming interface (API) calls and run key-loading scripts without asking. Load keys at runtime, never print or commit them, keep each within its owner's scope and existing budgets, and cap and cost-estimate key-billed batch or unattended runs. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-9)

10. **Explain terminology.** Expand every acronym, metric symbol and project-specific term on first use in each response, chat included; use descriptive names, not opaque internal labels. For Brando, a code may lead if a short gloss follows on first use. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-10)

11. **Numbers with verdicts.** Compact entries link full statistics (Rule 4). Give measured values, scales, denominators/splits, threshold sources, missing measurements. Statistical headlines need 95% intervals (resampling unit, limits) and `x [lo, hi] p-val=Z` (named test/null or `p-val=n/a`). Report correlations individually; when interpreting score levels, add absolute agreement and mean bias (judge minus human, positive = lenient) with both means. Give repeated-score variability/counts. Existing data only; read the statistics workflow first. Research precision (10-24-2026): read settings, definitions, numbers from the repo, run records or paper; `unknown` only after a named-path search (in caption). VeriBench tables carry a Pi + best open-weight row. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-11)

content.content:
## Hard Rule 3

3. **QA is explicit opt-in: run it only when Brando asks for it.** QA here means a model-reviewer pass (quality assurance, QA). It runs only when Brando explicitly requests a tier -- "do QA" / "QA it" / "light QA" (one review round), "mega QA" and the other Trigger Rule 10 phrases (the sequential chain) -- or when a runbook or commit tag he set names the tier (for example `[mega-qa]`). No agent starts a reviewer on its own: not for code, shared rules, claims/results, pushes to `main`, end-of-day or "high-stakes" moments, and not because a hook, a project file or an older rule text says QA is "required". **No repo-level hook may force QA on push** (Brando, 2026-09-15: "no repo in my computer should be doing a qa automatically"): a `git push` / `gh pr merge` gate in `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/*`, `.git/hooks/*` or CI must stay silent unless a tier was explicitly requested through an opt-in Brando set (env flag such as `<PROJ>_LIGHT_QA=1` / `<PROJ>_MEGA_QA=1`, or a `[qa]` / `[light-qa]` / `[mega-qa]` commit tag); a hook that blocks pushes by default is a bug to fix in that repo, not a rule to obey. **Without a request, still verify the work deterministically** before reporting done -- self-review the diff, `git diff --check`, and the relevant tests / compile / render / targeted grep. **Do not mention QA at all when none was requested** -- no "no QA was run" / "No QA was requested or run" line in replies, checkpoints or commit messages (Brando, 09-16-2026: "The default if qa's aren't the default is to not mention them at all"; the earlier "say in the reply that no QA was run" clause made every reply carry that sentence and was removed). **When QA is requested:** "do QA" or "light QA" = ONE opposite-agent round (Claude Code built -> Codex reviews; Codex built -> Claude Code reviews), the builder applies the findings, verifies them with deterministic checks, done; no automatic re-review. A second round or more only if Brando asks ("otherwise I run out of tokens", 2026-08-20). "mega QA" = Trigger Rule 10. **Separate acceptance requirements are not QA and are unchanged:** benchmark reference (gold) edits still need both model families (Trigger Rule 43), and a scientific model pin or an explicitly required reviewer family stays binding. **Why:** Brando, 09-14-2026: "can we make the qa rule in ac always explicit. I need to say do qa, mega or light for it to be triggered." **CLI-only, no API keys.** Any reviewer dispatch must use locally logged-in approved CLIs (`codex`, `clauded`) with cached subscription/OAuth credentials; never fall back to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY`. The deprecated Gemini CLI must not be used. Claude and Codex remain the preferred review families; Brando's September 11 cross-provider recovery authorization also permits other verified subscription clients under Trigger Rule 48 where the canonical review procedure allows them. Explicit required families and benchmark-reference acceptance are unchanged. See [`workflows/qa-correctness.md`](../workflows/qa-correctness.md) for tiers and [`workflows/qa-structural.md`](../workflows/qa-structural.md) for structural checks.

## Hard Rule 8

8. **Strong masters; proportionate execution workers; bounded review and quota recovery.** Keep the strongest configured model for masters and reasoning-critical work. A master explicitly chooses each worker's model and effort for its phase; capable regular workers are the default for well-specified execution. A detailed handoff reduces ambiguity, not the required standard of correctness. Do not lower global defaults to dispatch a worker. Trigger Rule 48 and [`workflows/reliable-agent-dispatch.md`](../workflows/reliable-agent-dispatch.md) define the completion budget, verified handoff and cross-provider recovery contract.
    - **Pinned defaults:** Codex `gpt-6-astra` with `model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"` in `~/.codex/config.toml`; dispatch with `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -m gpt-6-astra -c 'model_reasoning_effort="ultra"' "$QA_PROMPT"`. Claude Code `claude-fable-5-1` with `"effortLevel": "max"` in `~/.claude/settings.json` ([template](../claude-code-settings.json)); dispatch with `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions --model claude-fable-5-1 --effort max` (`claude-fable-5-1[1m]` for the one-million-token context variant). For a review that must not edit, put that constraint in the review brief while retaining full launch access under Trigger Rule 51; `--full-auto` is removed. Follow Trigger Rule 42 for unattended worker permissions and isolation.
    - **Worker selection:** separate planning, routine execution, the model being measured, and acceptance review. Prefer direct commands for deterministic work; for bounded implementation or research with clear inputs/tests, select a regular reasoning worker and supported effort explicitly. Escalate difficult decisions to the master or a stronger worker based on evidence. Reserve shared subscription allowance for remaining work, reviews and publication; do not send every remote worker at the master's maximum effort. after = json.loads((EXP / "support/sheet_exports/11-11-2026_final_form/after.json").read_text())
before = json.loads((EXP / "support/sheet_exports/11-11-2026_final_form/before.json").read_text())
print("after entry keys:", list(after[0].keys()))
print("before entry keys:", list(before[0].keys()))
for a in after:
    kinds = []
    for r in a.get("requests", []):
        k = list(r)[0]; d = r[k]
        extra = ""
        if k == "deleteDimension": extra = f"{d['range']['dimension']} {d['range']['startIndex']}-{d['range']['endIndex']}"
        if k == "updateDimensionProperties": extra = f"{d['range']['dimension']} {d['range'].get('startIndex')}-{d['range'].get('endIndex')} {d.get('properties')}"
        if k == "updateCells": extra = f"rows {d['range'].get('startRowIndex')}-{d['range'].get('endRowIndex')} cols {d['range'].get('startColumnIndex')}-{d['range'].get('endColumnIndex')} fields={d.get('fields')}"
        if k == "insertDimension": extra = f"{d['range']['dimension']} {d['range']['startIndex']}-{d['range']['endIndex']}"
        kinds.append(f"{k}({extra})")
    # equality
    eq = {k: v for k, v in a.items() if k not in ("requests", "expected", "returned", "meta", "readback")}
    # compare expected with current csv
    rows = list(csv.reader(open(EXP / "ratings" / a["filename"], newline=""))) if (EXP / "ratings" / a["filename"]).exists() else None
    match = rows is not None and rows[1:] == a["expected"]
    print(f"\n{a['filename']}: csv_matches_expected={match} flags={eq}")
    print("  requests:", "; ".join(kinds)[:900])
EOF

"""Regression checks for the common form and preservation of new metadata."""
import csv
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import unittest
from zipfile import ZipFile

EXP = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def load(name, path):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod


IMPORTER = load("form_import", EXP / "support/scripts/legacy/import_rating_sheet.py")
REVISION = load("form_packet", EXP / "support/scripts/revise_rating_packet.py")


class FormRevisionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_time_estimates_accept_ranges_without_inventing_a_point_estimate(self):
        for answer, valid in [("5-10", True), ("5–10", True), ("0", True), ("2.5", True),
                              ("10-5", False), ("-1", False), ("nan", False), ("inf", False)]:
            text = "rater_id,item_id,final_score_0_5,minutes_spent\nA1,N01a,2," + answer + "\n"
            rows, errors, _, _, _ = IMPORTER.check(text, "A1", {"N01a"}, None, "setN")
            self.assertEqual(not errors, valid, answer)
            if valid:
                self.assertEqual(rows[0]["minutes_spent"], answer)

    def test_descriptive_questions_match_guide_and_validate_like_legacy(self):
        schema = json.loads((EXP / "support/RATING_FORM_SCHEMA.json").read_text())
        guide = (EXP / "rating_task_packet/RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md").read_text()
        aliases = schema["legacy_checklist_headers"]
        self.assertEqual(schema["columns"][5:7], schema["required_new_responses"])
        self.assertEqual(schema["optional"], ["rationale", "problem_note"])
        self.assertEqual(schema["recommended"], ["minutes_spent", "confidence", "rationale"])
        for field in schema["required_new_responses"]:
            self.assertIn(field, guide)
        fields = ["rater_id", "item_id", "final_score_0_5", *aliases.values()]
        for answer, invalid in [("yes", False), ("invalid", True)]:
            buf = io.StringIO()
            w = csv.writer(buf)
            w.writerow(fields)
            w.writerow(["A1", "W01a", "2", answer, "no", "yes", "handful"])
            rows, errors, _, _, _ = IMPORTER.check(buf.getvalue(), "A1", {"W01a"}, None, "warmup")
            self.assertEqual(bool(errors), invalid)
            if not invalid:
                self.assertEqual(rows[0][aliases["A"]], "y")
                self.assertEqual(rows[0][aliases["D"]], "handful")

    def test_required_only_submission_preserves_scoring_sections(self):
        original = (EXP / "support/sheet_exports/11-11-2026_required_only/previous_human_judgements_prompt.md").read_text()
        updated = REVISION.current_form_rubric(original)
        self.assertEqual(original.split("## Output format")[0], updated.split("## Output format")[0])
        self.assertEqual(original.split("## Tie-break rule")[1], updated.split("## Tie-break rule")[1])
        self.assertNotIn("Optional notes", updated)

    def test_name_first_sheet_with_shifted_comment_and_multiline_note(self):
        fields = ["rater_name", "rater_id", "item_id", "final_score_0_5", "problem_note"]
        buf = io.StringIO()
        writer = csv.writer(buf)
        writer.writerow(["", "# TLDR: existing sheet comment", "context"])
        writer.writerow(fields)
        writer.writerow(["Brando Miranda", "A1", "N01a", "0", "First line\n# literal note"])
        submitted, parsed = IMPORTER.read_rows(buf.getvalue())
        self.assertEqual(submitted, fields)
        self.assertEqual(parsed[0]["problem_note"], "First line\n# literal note")
        rows, errors, _, _, _ = IMPORTER.check(buf.getvalue(), "A1", {"N01a"}, None, "setN")
        self.assertFalse(errors)
        data = IMPORTER.normalized_csv(rows, ["rater_id", "item_id", "final_score_0_5"], submitted)
        reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(data.decode()))
        self.assertEqual(reader.fieldnames[:2], ["rater_name", "rater_id"])
        row = next(reader)
        self.assertEqual(row["rater_name"], "Brando Miranda")
        self.assertEqual(row["final_score_0_5"], "0")
        self.assertEqual(row["problem_note"], "First line\n# literal note")

    def test_descriptive_background_once_or_with_legacy_labels_is_preserved(self):
        detail = "Lean tutorial; wrote 5 small proofs, about 10 hours last year."
        fields = ["rater_id", "item_id", "final_score_0_5", "lean_familiarity"]
        for later in ("", "Some"):
            buf = io.StringIO()
            w = csv.writer(buf)
            w.writerow(fields)
            w.writerow(["A1", "N01a", "2", detail])
            w.writerow(["A1", "N01b", "3", later])
            rows, errors, warnings, _, _ = IMPORTER.check(buf.getvalue(), "A1", {"N01a", "N01b"}, None, "setN")
            self.assertFalse(errors)
            self.assertEqual(rows[0]["lean_familiarity"], detail)
            self.assertEqual(rows[1]["lean_familiarity"], later.lower())
            self.assertEqual(bool(warnings), bool(later))
            data = IMPORTER.normalized_csv(rows, fields[:3], fields)
            self.assertEqual(next(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(data.decode())))["lean_familiarity"], detail)

    def test_metadata_survives_import_and_missing_attestation_is_not_fabricated(self):
        fields = ["rater_id", "item_id", "final_score_0_5", "model_assistance", "independent_rating_attestation"]
        buf = io.StringIO()
        w = csv.writer(buf)
        w.writerow(fields)
        w.writerow(["A1", "N01a", "0", "Claude: Lean notation", ""])
        rows, errors, warnings, _, _ = IMPORTER.check(buf.getvalue(), "A1", {"N01a"}, None, "setN")
        self.assertFalse(errors)
        self.assertTrue(any("attestation" in x for x in warnings))
        encoded = IMPORTER.normalized_csv(rows, fields[:3], fields)
        result = list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(encoded.decode())))[0]
        self.assertEqual(result["model_assistance"], "Claude: Lean notation")
        self.assertEqual(result["independent_rating_attestation"], "")
        self.assertEqual(result["final_score_0_5"], "0")

    def test_no_attestation_is_retained_and_flagged_not_dropped(self):
        text = "rater_id,item_id,final_score_0_5,model_assistance,independent_rating_attestation\nA1,N01a,2,help,no\n"
        rows, errors, warnings, _, _ = IMPORTER.check(text, "A1", {"N01a"}, None, "setN")
        self.assertFalse(errors)
        self.assertEqual(rows[0]["independent_rating_attestation"], "no")
        self.assertTrue(any("coordinator review" in x for x in warnings))

    def test_combined_attestation_preserves_honest_answers_without_legacy_requirement(self):
        for answer in ("yes", "no", "unsure", ""):
            text = "rater_id,item_id,final_score_0_5,ai_assisted_rating_attestation\nA1,N01a,2," + answer + "\n"
            rows, errors, warnings, _, _ = IMPORTER.check(text, "A1", {"N01a"}, None, "setN")
            self.assertFalse(errors)
            self.assertEqual(rows[0]["ai_assisted_rating_attestation"], answer)
            self.assertFalse(any("model_assistance" in w for w in warnings))
            self.assertEqual(bool(warnings), answer != "yes")
        legacy = "rater_id,item_id,final_score_0_5,independent_rating_attestation\nA1,N01a,2,yes\n"
        rows, _, _, _, _ = IMPORTER.check(legacy, "A1", {"N01a"}, None, "setN")
        self.assertNotIn("ai_assisted_rating_attestation", rows[0])

    def test_revised_archive_preserves_scientific_bytes_and_refuses_overwrite(self):
        files = {"START_HERE.md": b"Old instructions\n", "YOUR_RATING_SHEET.txt": b"Old link\n",
                 "human_judgements_prompt.md": b"Unchanged rubric\n",
                 "W01/python_source/task.py": b"# synthetic source\n",
                 "W01/gold_lean/task.lean": b"-- synthetic reference\n",
                 "W01/agent_lean/W01a.lean": b"-- synthetic candidate\n"}
        files["FILES.sha256"] = "".join(f"{hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()}  {n}\n" for n,b in sorted(files.items())).encode()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            src, dst = Path(td)/"original.zip", Path(td)/"revised.zip"
            with ZipFile(src,"w") as z:
                for n,b in files.items():z.writestr("original/"+n,b)
            original = src.read_bytes()
            receipt = REVISION.revise(src,dst,"A1","https://example.invalid/sheet")
            self.assertEqual(src.read_bytes(), original)
            self.assertEqual(receipt["preserved_scientific_files"],3)
            with ZipFile(dst) as z:
                self.assertNotIn("revised/YOUR_RATING_SHEET.txt", z.namelist())
                self.assertIn("https://example.invalid/sheet", z.read("revised/START_HERE.md").decode())
                for n,b in files.items():
                    if n.endswith((".lean",".py")):
                        mapped = json.loads((EXP/"support/WARMUP_PATHS.json").read_text())["paths"].get(n, n)
                        self.assertEqual(z.read("revised/"+mapped),b)
                reader=csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(z.read("revised/ratings.csv").decode()))
                self.assertEqual(reader.fieldnames,json.loads((EXP/"support/RATING_FORM_SCHEMA.json").read_text())["columns"])
                row=next(reader)
                self.assertEqual(reader.fieldnames[:2],["rater_name","rater_id"])
                self.assertEqual(row["rater_name"],"Brando Miranda")
                self.assertEqual(row["rater_id"],"A1")
                self.assertEqual(row["item_id"],"W01a")
                self.assertEqual(row["ai_assisted_rating_attestation"],"")
            with self.assertRaises(FileExistsError):
                REVISION.revise(src,dst,"A1","https://example.invalid/sheet")
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "verified name"):
                REVISION.revise(src,Path(td)/"unknown.zip","UNKNOWN","https://example.invalid/sheet")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Package assigned folders from the frozen human-rating delivery with a blank sheet."""

import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import io
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
from zipfile import ZIP_DEFLATED, ZipFile
from revise_rating_packet import current_form_rubric

MANIFEST_SHA256 = "0e4166045463dac71c2d7e70702f9c8b58ffccedeacdbff13ef4e57b8e85efa4"
FORM_HOME = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
COLUMNS = json.loads((FORM_HOME / "support/RATING_FORM_SCHEMA.json").read_text())["columns"]


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("source", type=Path, help="Extracted original personal packet")
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path, help="New team ZIP file")
    parser.add_argument("--rater", help="Verified rater ID to prefill the name and ID; omit only for an unassigned template")
    parser.add_argument("--folders", nargs="+", type=int, choices=range(1, 26),
                        default=range(1, 26), metavar="1..25")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    identities = json.loads((FORM_HOME / "support/RATER_IDENTITIES.json").read_text())
    if args.rater and args.rater not in identities:
        parser.error("Unknown rater; add the verified name to RATER_IDENTITIES.json first.")
    rater_name = identities[args.rater]["rater_name"] if args.rater else ""
    manifest = (args.source / "FILES.sha256").read_bytes()
    if hashlib.sha256(manifest).hexdigest() != MANIFEST_SHA256:
        parser.error("Source manifest differs from the frozen delivery.")

    folders = {f"Files_To_Rate{number:02}" for number in args.folders}
    members = {}
    rows = []
    for line in manifest.decode().splitlines():
        digest, name = line.split("  ", 1)
        path = Path(name)
        if path.parts[0] not in folders and name not in {"Rating_Instructions.md", "START_HERE.md"}:
            continue
        data = (args.source / path).read_bytes()
        if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != digest:
            parser.error(f"Source file differs from its delivery manifest: {name}")
        members[name] = data
        if path.parent.name == "agent_lean":
            rows.append({"rater_name": rater_name, "rater_id": args.rater or "",
                         "item_id": path.stem, "task_folder": path.parts[0], "candidate_file": path.name})

    schema = json.loads((FORM_HOME / "support/RATING_FORM_SCHEMA.json").read_text())
    guide = (FORM_HOME / "rating_task_packet/RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md").read_text()
    if any(field not in guide for field in schema["required_new_responses"]):
        raise ValueError("Form guide does not match required response fields")
    if len(rows) != 5 * len(folders):
        parser.error("Unexpected candidate count.")
    rubric = re.sub(r"^Open \[your personal rating sheet\].+$",
                    "Fill the assigned ratings.csv form.", members["Rating_Instructions.md"].decode(), flags=re.MULTILINE)
    members["Rating_Instructions.md"] = current_form_rubric(rubric).encode()
    members["START_HERE.md"] = (
        "# Rate theorem coverage\n\n"
        "Read RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md first for the current fields and assistance policy; "
        "it supersedes older submission/assistance instructions below.\n\n"
        "Read Rating_Instructions.md. In each assigned folder, read the Python source and the "
        "gold Lean theorem statements, then rate each candidate under agent_lean. The files in "
        "gold_lean_dependencies, when present, support the reference.\n\n"
        "Open ratings.csv in a spreadsheet editor. Check your name and rater ID, then enter final_score_0_5 "
        "and ai_assisted_rating_attestation for each assigned file. Please estimate minutes_spent and confidence; rationale is preferred but optional. Use problem_note for issues. "
        "Keep the prefilled identifiers intact. Email reference problems to Brando. "
        "Return your completed CSV privately to Brando.\n"
    ).encode()
    members["RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md"] = (FORM_HOME / "rating_task_packet/RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md").read_bytes()
    sheet = io.StringIO(newline="")
    writer = csv.DictWriter(sheet, fieldnames=COLUMNS)
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(rows)
    members["ratings.csv"] = sheet.getvalue().encode()
    members["FILES.sha256"] = "".join(
        f"{hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()}  {name}\n" for name, data in sorted(members.items())
    ).encode()
    with ZipFile(args.output, "x", compression=ZIP_DEFLATED) as archive:
        for name, data in sorted(members.items()):
            archive.writestr(name, data)
    print(f"{args.output}: {len(folders)} folders, {len(rows)} candidates")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Create a versioned common-form packet from an immutable delivered archive."""
import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import io
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
from zipfile import ZipFile, ZIP_DEFLATED

HOME = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def current_form_rubric(text):
    """Update submission directions only; preserve every scoring section verbatim."""
    output = ("## Output format (required)\n\n"
              "Use your personal sheet linked in START_HERE.md, or the assigned ratings.csv return route. "
              "Enter final_score_0_5 and ai_assisted_rating_attestation. Please estimate minutes_spent and confidence. A one-sentence rationale is preferred but optional; use problem_note for issues. "
              "RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md explains these answers. Identifiers are prefilled. "
              "The checklist and base score remain scoring steps, not separate form entries.\n\n")
    text = re.sub(r"## Current form headers[\s\S]*$", "", text)
    if "## Output format (required)" in text:
        text, count = re.subn(r"## Output format \(required\)[\s\S]*?(?=## Tie-break rule)", lambda _: output, text)
        if count != 1:
            raise ValueError("Unexpected rubric output section")
        return text
    return text + "\n\n" + output


def revise(source, output, rater, sheet_url):
    schema = json.loads((HOME / "support/RATING_FORM_SCHEMA.json").read_text())
    guide = (HOME / "rating_task_packet/RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md").read_text()
    if any(field not in guide for field in schema["required_new_responses"]):
        raise ValueError("Form guide does not match required response fields")
    identities = json.loads((HOME / "support/RATER_IDENTITIES.json").read_text())
    if rater not in identities or not identities[rater]["rater_name"].strip():
        raise ValueError(f"No verified name for {rater}; update RATER_IDENTITIES.json first")
    rater_name = identities[rater]["rater_name"]
    with ZipFile(source) as z:
        raw = {n: z.read(n) for n in z.namelist() if not n.endswith("/")}
    roots = {n.split("/")[0] for n in raw}
    root = next(iter(roots)) + "/" if len(roots) == 1 and all("/" in n for n in raw) else ""
    files = {n[len(root):]: b for n, b in raw.items()}
    listing = dict((n, digest) for digest, n in
                   (line.split("  ", 1) for line in files["FILES.sha256"].decode().splitlines() if line.strip()))
    for n, digest in listing.items():
        if hashlib.sha256(files[n]).hexdigest() != digest:
            raise ValueError(f"Source hash mismatch: {n}")
    path_map = json.loads((HOME / "support/WARMUP_PATHS.json").read_text())["paths"]
    original_names = {path_map.get(n, n): n for n in files}
    files = {path_map.get(n, n): b for n, b in files.items()}
    candidates = sorted((n for n in files if "/agent_lean/" in n and n.endswith(".lean")),
                        key=lambda n: [int(x) if x.isdigit() else x for x in re.split(r"(\d+)", n)])
    if not candidates:
        raise ValueError("No candidates")
    rubric = "Rating_Instructions.md" if "Rating_Instructions.md" in files else "human_judgements_prompt.md"
    files[rubric] = current_form_rubric(files[rubric].decode()).encode()
    # Delivered scientific payload is copied byte-for-byte, never regenerated.
    protected = {n: b for n, b in files.items() if n.endswith((".lean", ".py"))}
    files["RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md"] = (HOME / "rating_task_packet/RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md").read_bytes()
    return_route = (f"1. [Open your personal Google Sheet]({sheet_url}) for {rater_name}. Use that existing sheet; no copy is needed.\n" if sheet_url else f"1. Open ratings.csv for {rater_name}. Return the completed CSV to brandojazz@gmail.com.\n")
    files["START_HERE.md"] = (
        "# Start your human ratings\n\n"
        f"This packet has {len(candidates)} candidate files. Form revision: 11-11-2026.\n\n"
        + return_route +
        "2. Read RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md for the shared warm-up/main fields and assistance policy. "
        "It supersedes older submission links and assistance wording.\n"
        f"3. Read {rubric} for the unchanged 0–5 scoring rubric. "
        "Read Python source, gold theorem statements and candidate theorem statements in each task folder. "
        "Rate statements, not proofs.\n"
        "4. Fill one row per candidate in your assigned form. Use AI for localized assistance. "
        "Make the comparison, choose the score and answer the attestation yourself. Please estimate minutes and confidence; a one-sentence rationale is preferred but optional. Add a problem note if needed.\n\n"
        + ("The included ratings.csv has the same columns; use your personal Google Sheet, not both.\n" if sheet_url else "Save and return the completed ratings.csv; you do not need a Google Sheet.\n")
    ).encode()
    # The personal link lives in START_HERE; remove the redundant legacy pointer.
    files.pop("YOUR_RATING_SHEET.txt", None)
    # Remove superseded blank form copies from the new archive only.
    for n in list(files):
        if n.endswith(".csv") and ("rating" in Path(n).name.lower()):
            del files[n]
    buf = io.StringIO(newline="")
    w = csv.DictWriter(buf, fieldnames=schema["columns"], lineterminator="\n")
    w.writeheader()
    for n in candidates:
        p = Path(n)
        w.writerow({"rater_name": rater_name, "rater_id": rater, "item_id": Path(original_names[n]).stem, "task_folder": p.parts[0],
                    "candidate_file": p.name if p.parts[0].startswith("Files_To_Rate") else n})
    files["ratings.csv"] = buf.getvalue().encode()
    files["FILES.sha256"] = "".join(
        f"{hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()}  {n}\n" for n, b in sorted(files.items())
        if n != "FILES.sha256").encode()
    with ZipFile(output, "x", compression=ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        for n, b in sorted(files.items()):
            z.writestr(output.stem + "/" + n, b)
    with ZipFile(output) as z:
        for n, b in protected.items():
            assert z.read(output.stem + "/" + n) == b
        for line in files["FILES.sha256"].decode().splitlines():
            digest, n = line.split("  ", 1)
            assert hashlib.sha256(z.read(output.stem + "/" + n)).hexdigest() == digest
    receipt = {"schema_version": schema["version"], "source": str(source),
               "source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(source.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
               "output": str(output), "output_sha256": hashlib.sha256(output.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
               "rater_name": rater_name, "rater_id": rater, "sheet_url": sheet_url, "candidate_count": len(candidates),
               "preserved_scientific_files": len(protected), "columns": schema["columns"]}
    output.with_suffix(".receipt.json").write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + "\n")
    return receipt


if __name__ == "__main__":
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument("source", type=Path)
    p.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    p.add_argument("--rater", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--sheet-url", help="Personal sheet; omit for an explicitly assigned CSV return route")
    a = p.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(revise(a.source, a.output, a.rater, a.sheet_url), indent=2))

from revise_rating_packet import current_form_rubric

    if len(rows) != 5 * len(folders):
        parser.error("Unexpected candidate count.")
    rubric = re.sub(r"^Open \[your personal rating sheet\].+$",
                    "Fill the assigned ratings.csv form.", members["Rating_Instructions.md"].decode(), flags=re.MULTILINE)
    members["Rating_Instructions.md"] = current_form_rubric(rubric).encode()
    members["START_HERE.md"] = (
        "# Rate theorem coverage\n\n"
        "Read RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md first for the current fields and assistance policy; "
        "it supersedes older submission/assistance instructions below.\n\n"
        "Read Rating_Instructions.md. In each assigned folder, read the Python source and the "
        "gold Lean theorem statements, then rate each candidate under agent_lean. The files in "
        "gold_lean_dependencies, when present, support the reference.\n\n"
        "Open ratings.csv in a spreadsheet editor. Check your name and rater ID, then enter final_score_0_5 "
        "and ai_assisted_rating_attestation for each assigned file. Please estimate minutes_spent and confidence; rationale is preferred but optional. Use problem_note for issues. "
        "Keep the prefilled identifiers intact. Email reference problems to Brando. "
        "Return your completed CSV privately to Brando.\n"
    ).encode()
    members["RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md"] = (FORM_HOME / "rating_task_packet/RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md").read_bytes()
    sheet = io.StringIO(newline="")
    writer = csv.DictWriter(sheet, fieldnames=COLUMNS)
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(rows)
    members["ratings.csv"] = sheet.getvalue().encode()
    members["FILES.sha256"] = "".join(
        f"{hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()}  {name}\n" for name, data in sorted(members.items())
    ).encode()
    with ZipFile(args.output, "x", compression=ZIP_DEFLATED) as archive:
        for name, data in sorted(members.items()):
            archive.writestr(name, data)
    print(f"{args.output}: {len(folders)} folders, {len(rows)} candidates")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Create a versioned common-form packet from an immutable delivered archive."""
import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import io
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
from zipfile import ZipFile, ZIP_DEFLATED

HOME = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def current_form_rubric(text):
    """Update submission directions only; preserve every scoring section verbatim."""
    output = ("## Output format (required)\n\n"
              "Use your personal sheet linked in START_HERE.md, or the assigned ratings.csv return route. "
              "Enter final_score_0_5 and ai_assisted_rating_attestation. Please estimate minutes_spent and confidence. A one-sentence rationale is preferred but optional; use problem_note for issues. "
              "RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md explains these answers. Identifiers are prefilled. "
              "The checklist and base score remain scoring steps, not separate form entries.\n\n")
    text = re.sub(r"## Current form headers[\s\S]*$", "", text)
    if "## Output format (required)" in text:
        text, count = re.subn(r"## Output format \(required\)[\s\S]*?(?=## Tie-break rule)", lambda _: output, text)
        if count != 1:
            raise ValueError("Unexpected rubric output section")
        return text
    return text + "\n\n" + output


def revise(source, output, rater, sheet_url):
    schema = json.loads((HOME / "support/RATING_FORM_SCHEMA.json").read_text())
    guide = (HOME / "rating_task_packet/RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md").read_text()
    if any(field not in guide for field in schema["required_new_responses"]):
        raise ValueError("Form guide does not match required response fields")
    identities = json.loads((HOME / "support/RATER_IDENTITIES.json").read_text())
    if rater not in identities or not identities[rater]["rater_name"].strip():
        raise ValueError(f"No verified name for {rater}; update RATER_IDENTITIES.json first")
    rater_name = identities[rater]["rater_name"]
    with ZipFile(source) as z:
        raw = {n: z.read(n) for n in z.namelist() if not n.endswith("/")}
    roots = {n.split("/")[0] for n in raw}
    root = next(iter(roots)) + "/" if len(roots) == 1 and all("/" in n for n in raw) else ""
    files = {n[len(root):]: b for n, b in raw.items()}
    listing = dict((n, digest) for digest, n in
                   (line.split("  ", 1) for line in files["FILES.sha256"].decode().splitlines() if line.strip()))
    for n, digest in listing.items():
        if hashlib.sha256(files[n]).hexdigest() != digest:
            raise ValueError(f"Source hash mismatch: {n}")
    path_map = json.loads((HOME / "support/WARMUP_PATHS.json").read_text())["paths"]
    original_names = {path_map.get(n, n): n for n in files}
    files = {path_map.get(n, n): b for n, b in files.items()}
    candidates = sorted((n for n in files if "/agent_lean/" in n and n.endswith(".lean")),
                        key=lambda n: [int(x) if x.isdigit() else x for x in re.split(r"(\d+)", n)])
    if not candidates:
        raise ValueError("No candidates")
    rubric = "Rating_Instructions.md" if "Rating_Instructions.md" in files else "human_judgements_prompt.md"
    files[rubric] = current_form_rubric(files[rubric].decode()).encode()
    # Delivered scientific payload is copied byte-for-byte, never regenerated.
    protected = {n: b for n, b in files.items() if n.endswith((".lean", ".py"))}
    files["RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md"] = (HOME / "rating_task_packet/RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md").read_bytes()
    return_route = (f"1. [Open your personal Google Sheet]({sheet_url}) for {rater_name}. Use that existing sheet; no copy is needed.\n" if sheet_url else f"1. Open ratings.csv for {rater_name}. Return the completed CSV to brandojazz@gmail.com.\n")
    files["START_HERE.md"] = (
        "# Start your human ratings\n\n"
        f"This packet has {len(candidates)} candidate files. Form revision: 11-11-2026.\n\n"
        + return_route +
        "2. Read RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md for the shared warm-up/main fields and assistance policy. "
        "It supersedes older submission links and assistance wording.\n"
        f"3. Read {rubric} for the unchanged 0–5 scoring rubric. "
        "Read Python source, gold theorem statements and candidate theorem statements in each task folder. "
        "Rate statements, not proofs.\n"
        "4. Fill one row per candidate in your assigned form. Use AI for localized assistance. "
        "Make the comparison, choose the score and answer the attestation yourself. Please estimate minutes and confidence; a one-sentence rationale is preferred but optional. Add a problem note if needed.\n\n"
        + ("The included ratings.csv has the same columns; use your personal Google Sheet, not both.\n" if sheet_url else "Save and return the completed ratings.csv; you do not need a Google Sheet.\n")
    ).encode()
    # The personal link lives in START_HERE; remove the redundant legacy pointer.
    files.pop("YOUR_RATING_SHEET.txt", None)
    # Remove superseded blank form copies from the new archive only.
    for n in list(files):
        if n.endswith(".csv") and ("rating" in Path(n).name.lower()):
            del files[n]
    buf = io.StringIO(newline="")
    w = csv.DictWriter(buf, fieldnames=schema["columns"], lineterminator="\n")
    w.writeheader()
    for n in candidates:
        p = Path(n)
        w.writerow({"rater_name": rater_name, "rater_id": rater, "item_id": Path(original_names[n]).stem, "task_folder": p.parts[0],
                    "candidate_file": p.name if p.parts[0].startswith("Files_To_Rate") else n})
    files["ratings.csv"] = buf.getvalue().encode()
    files["FILES.sha256"] = "".join(
        f"{hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()}  {n}\n" for n, b in sorted(files.items())
        if n != "FILES.sha256").encode()
    with ZipFile(output, "x", compression=ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        for n, b in sorted(files.items()):
            z.writestr(output.stem + "/" + n, b)
    with ZipFile(output) as z:
        for n, b in protected.items():
            assert z.read(output.stem + "/" + n) == b
        for line in files["FILES.sha256"].decode().splitlines():
            digest, n = line.split("  ", 1)
            assert hashlib.sha256(z.read(output.stem + "/" + n)).hexdigest() == digest
    receipt = {"schema_version": schema["version"], "source": str(source),
               "source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(source.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
               "output": str(output), "output_sha256": hashlib.sha256(output.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
               "rater_name": rater_name, "rater_id": rater, "sheet_url": sheet_url, "candidate_count": len(candidates),
               "preserved_scientific_files": len(protected), "columns": schema["columns"]}
    output.with_suffix(".receipt.json").write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + "\n")
    return receipt


if __name__ == "__main__":
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument("source", type=Path)
    p.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    p.add_argument("--rater", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--sheet-url", help="Personal sheet; omit for an explicitly assigned CSV return route")
    a = p.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(revise(a.source, a.output, a.rater, a.sheet_url), indent=2))

import re, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
repo = Path(sys.argv[1])
words = set(w.strip().lower() for w in open('/usr/share/dict/words'))
files = [f for f in subprocess.run(["git","diff","--name-only"],cwd=repo,capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.split() if f.endswith(".md")]
files += ["experiments/09_human_rating_collection/support/sheet_exports/11-11-2026_final_form/README.md",
          "private/09_human_rating_collection/preparation_11-09-2026/REVIEW_TEAM_EMAILS_FORM_V5.md"]
known = set("""veribench lean brando miranda rylan schaeffer srivatsava daruru sri yegor denisov blanch dilara soylu allen nie donald poindexter simon obstbaum nikil ravi slava naprienko codex tldr csv csvs json md zip readme url urls gmail edu www https http github gid prefilled unproved formv5 formv2 formv3 attestation attestations sha256 setn n17 n21 n01 n23 warmup rps ce tvd llm llms veribench's rater raters rubric unsent readback gcd ints floats nan sorry gcd_zero_thm
""".split())
import collections
for f in files:
    p = repo / f
    if not p.exists(): continue
    text = p.read_text()
    text = re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", " ", text); text = re.sub(r"https?://\S+", " ", text); text = re.sub(r"\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)", lambda m: m.group(0).split("]")[0][1:], text)
    bad = collections.Counter()
    for w in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z'’-]+", text):
        lw = w.lower().strip("'’-").replace("’", "'")
        base = lw.rstrip("s") if lw.endswith("s") else lw
        if lw in words or base in words or lw in known or base in known or "_" in w or w.isupper(): continue
        if any(x in lw for x in ("-", "'")): 
            parts = re.split(r"[-']", lw)
            if all(pp in words or pp in known or not pp for pp in parts): continue
        bad[w] += 1
    if bad: print(f"{f}: {sorted(bad)}")
EOF

 **TLDR:** Move the active human-rating collection from VeriBench into this experiment without changing delivered materials, opening sealed ratings, or conflating the inherited round with the prospective study.
 
-## State
+## Current preparation — 11-11-2026
+
+Use [the experiment README](../README.md) and [the current preparation section](PREPARATION_11-09-2026.md#current-prepared-version--11-11-2026). The working packet is in `../rating_task_packet/`; current raw data is in `../ratings/`; scripts/tests are in `scripts/` and `tests/` relative to this support folder. All twelve sheets and raw exports now share eleven columns: name, four stable identifiers, score, combined attestation, minutes, confidence, rationale and problem note. Rationale is preferred but optional. New required AI assistance is prospective; original human notes and times were restored verbatim, without inferred responses.
+
+Thirteen replacement packets and eight exact team email previews are prepared. Older drafts are historical; CURRENT_PREPARATION.json in the private preparation folder selects FormV5. Nothing has been sent in this revision. Brando's pilot, revised-text approval and explicit send instruction remain before team dispatch. Collection counts remain 15 numeric warm-ups, three N/A entries and no completed main ratings. Preserve the existing assigned subsets and prior-exposure history.
+
+## Historical migration state
